# Toric code — Level-2 map

This index separates proofs, decoder assumptions, operation protocols, and
hardware evidence. Each page answers one question completely and states which
facts are algebraic, machine-recomputed, or literature-claimed.

1. [Why the square torus gives [[2L²,2,L]]](homology-and-distance.md): cell
   counts, CSS commutation, the two global check dependencies, homology, and
   matching upper and lower distance bounds.
2. [Why cyclic HGP is exactly the Toric matrix](cyclic-hgp.md): the square
   cyclic parity maps, HGP block order, two kernel sectors, exact constructor
   equality, and the contrast with open Surface factors.
3. [Why syndrome is only the boundary of an error chain](syndrome-decoding.md):
   endpoint cancellation, homology-class ambiguity, perfect and noisy records,
   loss and coherent-noise boundaries, and decoder objectives.
4. [Which threshold a Toric number refers to](threshold-ledger.md): selected
   primary-source tuples and the reason no scalar belongs to the bare code.
5. [Which operations are verified and what hardware demonstrated](operations-and-realizations.md):
   logical loops, stacked-block CNOT, proposed Clifford protocols,
   non-Clifford boundaries, state preparation, and repeated correction.
6. [What each representation preserves](representations.md): chain, symplectic,
   anyon, HGP, statistical, PEPS, and Majorana dictionaries.

## Reproduction contract

Run from the repository root:

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
python atlas/toric/pedagogy/reproduce.py
make verify-entry E=atlas/toric
```

The same computation can be launched from a Python session:

```python
from runpy import run_path

run_path("atlas/toric/pedagogy/reproduce.py", run_name="__main__")
```

`reproduce.py` imports the shipped constructor and asserts the parameter
refusal boundary, cell counts, check ranks, row weights, CSS commutation,
global dependencies, exact small distances, four logical supports, periodic
scene contract, endpoint-syndrome walk, exact cyclic-HGP matrix equality, and
the two-block transversal-CNOT symplectic action. It exits nonzero on the first
disagreement. The entry verifier independently recomputes every claim in
`instances.yaml`.

The provenance split is deliberate:

- `n`, `k`, CSS structure, the committed small distances, logical supports,
  cyclic-HGP equality, and stacked-block CNOT are machine-verified.
- The all-`L` distance lower bound is a worked homological proof backed by the
  primary Toric literature.
- Decoder thresholds, proposed Clifford gadgets, and hardware results do not
  follow from a check matrix. They remain literature claims with their full
  model or protocol identity written beside them.
# Why the square torus gives `[[2L²,2,L]]`

## Statement and scope

For integer `L >= 2`, take an `L`-by-`L` square fundamental domain and identify
opposite sides. Put one qubit on each horizontal and vertical edge, an `X`
check at each vertex, and a `Z` check on each face boundary. The result has
`n=2L²`, `k=2`, and `d=L` [Kitaev 1997; Kitaev 2003;
Dennis et al. 2002]. The proof below is for this square cellulation, not an
arbitrary torus mesh.

## From cells to commuting checks

Let `C2`, `C1`, and `C0` be the binary spaces generated by faces, edges, and
vertices. Define

```text
C2 --d2--> C1 --d1--> C0 .
```

Each column of `d2` marks the four boundary edges of one face. Each column of
`d1` marks the two endpoints of one edge. At a corner of a face, exactly two
of its boundary edges touch that vertex. Therefore every entry of `d1 d2` is
zero modulo two. The constructor checks this matrix identity directly.

Set `HX=d1` and `HZ=d2^T`. Then

```text
HX HZ^T = d1 d2 = 0,
```

so every `X` star commutes with every `Z` plaquette. In Pauli language a
neighboring pair overlaps on two qubits, producing two anticommutation signs;
a non-neighboring pair overlaps on none.

## Cell count and stabilizer rank

The periodic domain has `L²` vertices and `L²` faces. Choose at every vertex
the horizontal edge leaving it and the vertical edge leaving it. This counts
each edge exactly once, so there are `2L²` edge qubits.

Every column of `d1` has two ones. Hence the sum of all vertex rows is zero.
To see that no further dependency exists, select a spanning tree of the
connected periodic graph. Its vertex-edge incidence matrix has rank `L²-1`:
starting at a leaf, its unique incident tree edge forces that leaf coefficient
to vanish in any row dependency; removing leaves iteratively leaves only the
global all-vertex relation. Thus `rank(HX)=L²-1`.

Apply the same argument to the connected dual graph. Faces are dual vertices
and primal edges are dual edges, so `rank(HZ)=L²-1`. The total stabilizer rank
is `2L²-2`, and

```text
k = n - rank(HX) - rank(HZ)
  = 2L² - (L²-1) - (L²-1)
  = 2.
```

This also identifies the two global dependencies: the product of every star
and the product of every plaquette are each identity because every qubit
appears twice.

## Homology gives the logical operators

A `Z` string is a binary edge chain. It commutes with all stars exactly when
its boundary is zero, so closed `Z` strings lie in `ker(d1)`. A product of
plaquettes is a face boundary in `im(d2)`. Therefore distinct `Z` logical
classes are

```text
H1(torus; GF(2)) = ker(d1) / im(d2).
```

There are two generators: one winds horizontally and one vertically. The dual
cellulation gives two `X` cycles. Choose each dual cycle to cross its conjugate
primal cycle once and the other primal cycle zero times. Odd intersection is
the symplectic product, so each selected `X`/`Z` pair anticommutes and the
cross-pairs commute.

The constructor exports exactly these four supports and refuses them if they
fail stabilizer commutation, fall inside the stabilizer row space, or have the
wrong four-by-four symplectic product matrix.

## Distance upper bound

A straight row of `L` horizontal edges winds once around the torus and is a
nontrivial `Z` cycle. A straight column of `L` vertical edges gives the other
`Z` class. Corresponding straight dual loops supply `X` logicals. Each has
weight `L`, so `d <= L`.

## Distance lower bound

Take a primal cycle with nonzero horizontal winding. Draw the `L` parallel
vertical dual cuts, one between each neighboring pair of vertex columns. A
horizontal-winding cycle has odd intersection with every cut. Each primal edge
can cross at most one such cut, so the cycle contains at least `L` edges. A
vertical-winding cycle obeys the rotated argument.

If a cycle has zero winding in both directions, it is a face boundary and is
not logical. Thus every nontrivial primal logical has weight at least `L`.
Repeating the cut argument on the dual lattice gives the same lower bound for
`X` logicals. Combining bounds yields `d=L`.

The `L=2` cellulation is small but still satisfies the argument: opposite
directions join the same two coordinate layers, yet the constructor keeps four
distinct incident edge qubits at every check and exact enumeration returns
distance two.

## Machine replay

`reproduce.py` checks `L=2,3,4` cell counts, ranks, row weights, global
dependencies, logical intersections, and periodic scene data. It invokes exact
distance enumeration for the two committed instances. The claims in
`instances.yaml` carry `{kind: verified}` and are independently recomputed by
`make verify-entry`.

Primary sources: `kitaev1997imperfect`, `kitaev1997quantum`,
`kitaev2003fault`, and `dennis2002topological`.

chunks.markdown: # Which operations are verified, and what did hardware demonstrate?

heading_path: Which operations are verified, and what did hardware demonstrate?
chunks.markdown:
## Constructor-verified logical Paulis

The constructor exports two primal `Z` cycles and two dual `X` cycles. For
each support it builds a binary symplectic row and verifies three conditions:

1. the row commutes with every stabilizer;
2. it is not in the stabilizer row space; and
3. the four rows have exactly two conjugate odd-intersection pairs.

Applying one string is a logical Pauli. Because its single-qubit factors can be
applied in parallel, the physical depth is one when the control hardware
allows simultaneous Paulis. In practice a decoded logical Pauli is usually
recorded in a classical Pauli frame, avoiding a physical layer.

The support has weight `L`; “depth one” does not mean “weight one” and does not
remove control, calibration, or correlated-fault concerns.

heading_path: Which operations are verified, and what did hardware demonstrate?
chunks.markdown:
## Verified stacked-block CNOT

Align two identical blocks and apply physical CNOT from each control edge to
the corresponding target edge. Pauli conjugation acts as

```text
Xc -> Xc Xt,   Xt -> Xt,
Zc -> Zc,      Zt -> Zc Zt.
```

An `X` star on the control becomes the product of corresponding stars on both
blocks; a target `Z` plaquette similarly becomes the product on both blocks.
The other two stabilizer sectors remain in place, so the joint stabilizer
group is preserved. Exactly the same mapping holds for each homological
logical pair, implementing CNOT separately on both encoded qubits.

`reproduce.py` constructs the doubled symplectic stabilizer space, performs
this conjugation, checks equality of row spaces, and checks every selected
logical generator. This proves the code-space action. It does not prove that a
given device can align blocks, suppress transport faults, or decode correlated
two-block events.

heading_path: Which operations are verified, and what did hardware demonstrate?
chunks.markdown:
## Claimed single-block Clifford protocol

`guernut2024toric` proposes and simulates a constant-depth Toric Clifford
toolkit combining fold-transversal gates, Dehn twists, and single-shot logical
Pauli measurements. These ingredients require geometric pairings,
cellulation-deformation schedules, ancillas, and decoding assumptions absent
from the static constructor. The card therefore marks the toolkit and logical
measurement as `{kind: claimed, ref: guernut2024toric}`.

`bravyi2013classification` supplies a boundary rather than an implementation:
locality-preserving constant-depth logical gates for two-dimensional
topological stabilizer codes are restricted to the Clifford level. A
non-Clifford protocol for a broader abelian phase may add twists or enriched
structure, as in `bauer2025nonclifford`; it is not a native operation of the
unmodified square Toric stabilizer. T144 consequently adds no bare `T` gate.

heading_path: Which operations are verified, and what did hardware demonstrate?
chunks.markdown:
## Hardware evidence ledger

| Source | Demonstrated object | Quantitative identity | Explicit non-claim |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bluvstein2022processor` | Neutral-atom preparation and characterization of a Toric-code state on periodic geometry | A twenty-four-qubit Toric state in the experiment's transported-atom processor | Not repeated syndrome extraction, arbitrary logical-state memory, or below-threshold scaling |
| `atomcomputing2026toric` | Repeated mid-circuit Toric syndrome extraction with lost-atom replacement and reservoir reloading | Logical error characterized through as many as ninety cycles; two code distances compared only through eight rounds, with lower absolute logical error for the larger distance in that range | Not an asymptotic or model-independent threshold claim |

Both rows are `demonstrated` because the reported protocols ran on hardware.
The descriptions remain different because demonstration status does not erase
the distinction between state preparation and active error correction.

heading_path: Which operations are verified, and what did hardware demonstrate?
chunks.markdown:
## Reader decision procedure

When encountering a Toric operation or experiment, ask in this order:

1. Is the statement only a logical symplectic action, or is there a physical
   protocol?
2. If physical, what geometry, ancilla, measurement, and decoder resources are
   assumed?
3. Is fault tolerance proved, simulated, or measured?
4. For hardware, was a code state prepared, were syndromes repeated, was an
   unknown logical state preserved, and was distance scaling established over
   a declared range?

This sequence prevents a valid algebraic gate from becoming an unsupported
hardware claim and prevents a finite experiment from becoming a universal
threshold statement.

Primary sources: `kitaev2003fault`, `bravyi2013classification`,
`guernut2024toric`, `bauer2025nonclifford`, `bluvstein2022processor`, and
`atomcomputing2026toric`.

heading_path: What does each Toric representation preserve?
chunks.markdown: # What does each Toric representation preserve?

heading_path: What does each Toric representation preserve?
chunks.markdown:
## One object, several dictionaries

The code is one stabilizer subspace, but different representations make
different invariants cheap to see. A responsible conversion states what is
preserved and what extra assumptions are introduced.

| Picture | Native object | Makes immediate | Does not provide by itself |
|---|---|---|---|
| Symplectic CSS | binary `HX`, `HZ` | commutation, rank, finite syndrome, row-space logical tests | geometry, circuit, or likelihood |
| Chain complex | `C2 -> C1 -> C0` | boundary cancellation, homology, primal/dual cycles | decoder probabilities or hardware schedule |
| Cyclic HGP | two square neighbor-parity maps | tensor-separated directions and two kernel sectors | identity with arbitrary HGP outputs |
| Anyon strings | charges, strings, intersections | endpoint motion, fusion, logical commutation | a finite check ordering or decoder runtime |
| Statistical mechanics | disorder sectors and partition functions | class likelihoods and phase transitions | one model-free threshold |
| PEPS | local tensors with virtual symmetry | topological degeneracy and local indistinguishability | active QEC or repeated syndrome circuits |
| Majorana simulation | quadratic fermionic evolution in restricted channels | efficient coherent-error calculation | a physical tetron realization or arbitrary coherent-noise decoder |

heading_path: What does each Toric representation preserve?
chunks.markdown:
## Symplectic and chain-complex equivalence

The constructor takes the face boundary `d2` and edge boundary `d1`, then
emits `HX=d1` and `HZ=d2^T`. This conversion preserves the exact qubit and
check order. The identity `d1 d2=0` becomes `HX HZ^T=0`; chain cycles become
commuting Pauli rows, and chain boundaries become stabilizer products.

The symplectic picture forgets why the matrices commute but is ideal for
machine checks. The chain picture restores the geometric reason and gives the
quotient `ker/im` that classifies logicals.

heading_path: What does each Toric representation preserve?
chunks.markdown:
## HGP is exact but factor-sensitive

The cyclic-HGP converter preserves the ordered matrices only for the stated
orientation `HGP(C_L,C_L^T)`. Open repetition factors change dimensions and
kernel sectors, producing the planar Surface witness. General HGP factors can
produce codes with no two-dimensional local embedding. The exact dictionary
therefore supports a typed construction relation, not a claim that Toric and
HGP are synonyms. See [cyclic HGP](cyclic-hgp.md).

heading_path: What does each Toric representation preserve?
chunks.markdown:
## Anyons and statistical mechanics

The anyon dictionary turns a violated star or plaquette into an endpoint
charge. Local Pauli errors create pairs; extending a string moves an endpoint;
closing and winding the string performs a logical. It preserves fusion and
intersection information but suppresses the row ordering used by software.

The statistical dictionary fixes a syndrome and groups compatible error
chains by homology. A disorder-sector partition function sums the probability
of a class. The critical point depends on the channel and syndrome model, so
the representation explains thresholds only after the model tuple is fixed.
`dennis2002topological` supplies the direct QEC mapping, while earlier Ising
papers remain classical precursors.

heading_path: What does each Toric representation preserve?
chunks.markdown:
## PEPS and Majorana boundaries

In a PEPS representation, a virtual `Z2` symmetry makes distinct torus sectors
locally indistinguishable and produces topological degeneracy
[`schuch2010peps`]. This is a ground-space representation. It does not imply
that preparing the PEPS, measuring syndromes fault tolerantly, and decoding a
memory are the same task.

For selected coherent channels, the correction calculation maps to free
Majorana fermions and admits efficient simulation [`bravyi2018coherent`].
`iverson2020coherence` gives a conditional logical-channel result and states
the fixed-noise-strength limitation. The mapping is therefore curated with
the `majorana-pairs` dialect and routed to `wanted:fermionic-compiler`; the
Atlas has no general executable converter for this view.

heading_path: What does each Toric representation preserve?
chunks.markdown:
## Relation boundary

Sharing a representation or bulk phase is weaker than code identity. The open
Surface entry shares star/plaquette bulk but changes boundary homology. The
Honeycomb protocol has Toric-equivalent instantaneous frames but remains a
periodic measurement process with an anyon automorphism. A broad `Z2`
topological phase can share anyon data while using a different microscopic
Hamiltonian or qubit layout. The Toric card keeps these as typed relations and
never expands its identity to absorb them.

Primary sources: `kitaev2003fault`, `dennis2002topological`,
`tillich2009quantum`, `schuch2010peps`, `bravyi2018coherent`,
`iverson2020coherence`, `hastings2021dynamically`, and
`aasen2022automorphism`.

heading_path: Why syndrome is only the boundary of an error chain
chunks.markdown: # Why syndrome is only the boundary of an error chain

heading_path: Why syndrome is only the boundary of an error chain
chunks.markdown:
## Algebraic syndrome

Write a Pauli error as binary vectors `(eX,eZ)` on the edge qubits. For the CSS
checks,

```text
star syndrome       sX = HX eZ,
plaquette syndrome  sZ = HZ eX,
```

with arithmetic modulo two. A single `Z` edge has the two endpoint vertices
in `sX`. Along a longer connected path, every internal vertex touches two
error edges and cancels; only the two endpoints remain. The dual statement
holds for an `X` path and plaquette defects.

heading_path: Why syndrome is only the boundary of an error chain
chunks.markdown:
## What the syndrome forgets

Suppose an error chain `e` and a candidate correction `c` have the same
boundary. Their sum `e+c` is closed. Three cases matter:

1. `e+c` bounds a collection of faces. It is a stabilizer, so the correction
   succeeds.
2. `e+c` has horizontal or vertical winding. It is a logical operator, so the
   correction returns to the code space but changes encoded information.
3. In a noisy measurement record, `e+c` is not a purely spatial chain at all;
   its endpoints and time boundary must be evaluated in the spacetime detector
   complex.

Thus decoding is a choice of logical class consistent with the data, not an
instruction to find any path between visible endpoints.

heading_path: Why syndrome is only the boundary of an error chain
chunks.markdown:
## Decoder objectives

Minimum-weight perfect matching assigns additive costs to graph edges, pairs
defects, and chooses one minimum-cost representative. It is efficient and
geometry-aware, but it does not sum all degenerate representatives in a class.
Maximum-likelihood decoding compares the total probability of logical classes;
in the statistical picture this is a free-energy rather than ground-energy
decision.

Renormalization-group decoders approximate class probabilities while merging
scales. Tensor-network methods contract a class partition function exactly for
restricted channels or approximately at controlled bond dimension. BP-OSD
uses generic sparse-matrix soft information and post-processing; it does not
automatically exploit periodic homology. A cellular automaton restricts
communication to a finite light cone and therefore solves an additional
locality problem.

heading_path: Why syndrome is only the boundary of an error chain
chunks.markdown:
## Regime map

| Regime | Decoder receives | Added ambiguity | Claim boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Code capacity | one perfect spatial syndrome and a Pauli prior | which spatial homology class | No measurement or circuit faults |
| Phenomenological | syndrome changes over repeated rounds | paths may run in time | Round count, time boundary, and data/check normalization matter |
| Circuit level | detector events from a named extraction circuit | correlated hooks, leakage, and schedule faults | A threshold belongs to that circuit and decoder |
| Detectable loss | syndrome plus known missing-edge locations | supercheck geometry and percolation | Known erasure is not unheralded leakage |
| Correlated Pauli | syndrome plus a joint prior | paths no longer have independent edge weights | Matching needs reweighting or a richer objective |
| Coherent rotation | amplitudes or a channel model, not only Pauli probabilities | interference between fault histories | Pauli twirling can change the logical channel |

heading_path: Why syndrome is only the boundary of an error chain
chunks.markdown:
## A reproducible endpoint walk

`reproduce.py` applies consecutive `Z` errors along one horizontal row. Every
proper open segment has exactly two star defects. Extending the segment by one
edge moves one endpoint. Completing all `L` edges closes a noncontractible
loop: the syndrome vanishes, yet the vector is outside the stabilizer row
space and equals a constructor-provided logical support.

This small experiment is the whole failure mechanism in miniature. The
decoder sees the same zero syndrome for identity, any stabilizer, and any
closed logical loop. Only the prior and error history distinguish them.

heading_path: Why syndrome is only the boundary of an error chain
chunks.markdown:
## Threshold discipline

The [threshold ledger](threshold-ledger.md) records source-reported values only
with channel, syndrome quality, decoder, and observable. It does not transfer
an open-Surface circuit number to the torus or compare a detectable-loss
percolation point with an unheralded Pauli rate.

Primary sources: `dennis2002topological`, `wang2003confinement`,
`wang2010thresholds`, `stace2009loss`, `duclos2010fast`,
`bravyi2014efficient`, `breuckmann2017local`, `chubb2021statistical`, and
`roffe2020decoding`.

heading_path: Which threshold does a Toric number refer to?
chunks.markdown: # Which threshold does a Toric number refer to?

heading_path: Which threshold does a Toric number refer to?
chunks.markdown:
## Rule

A threshold is a transition of a family of experiments, not an invariant of a
finite check matrix. Its identity tuple is

```text
(family and boundary, physical channel, syndrome/circuit model,
 decoder and objective, rate normalization, asymptotic observable).
```

Changing any coordinate can change the value. The Toric card therefore names
decoder regimes without putting one number in the entry summary.

heading_path: Which threshold does a Toric number refer to?
chunks.markdown:
## Selected primary-source tuples

Every value below has origin `{kind: claimed, ref: BIBKEY}`. None is recomputed
by the Atlas constructor.

| Source-reported value | Identity tuple | What may be concluded |
|---|---|---|
| `15.5%` | Periodic Toric family; ideal syndrome extraction; each data qubit receives `X`, `Y`, or `Z` with probability `p0/3`; graph matching; the paper converts the `X`-component rate to `p=(2/3)p0`; asymptotic logical transition | A benchmark in the paper's total single-qubit depolarizing-rate convention, not the independent-`X/Z` maximum-likelihood value from another convention. Origin: `wang2010thresholds`. |
| `7.8 × 10^-3` | Periodic Toric family; the named four-interaction-order extraction circuit; preparation, readout, memory, and two-qubit processes each assigned rate `p`, with the fifteen nonidentity two-qubit Paulis equiprobable after an ideal CNOT; repeated graph matching; asymptotic memory transition | A circuit-level result in that paper's equal-process-rate units, not a code-capacity or generic modern circuit threshold. Origin: `wang2010thresholds`. |
| `18.9(3)%` | Toric code; iid single-qubit depolarizing channel; correlations between `X`, `Y`, and `Z` components retained through an eight-vertex-model mapping; optimal-class transition | A depolarizing-channel threshold under the paper's correlated Pauli convention, not three independent binary matching problems. Origin: `bombin2012strong`. |
| `50%` detectable loss | Square-lattice topological code; erasure locations known; loss geometry controlled by bond percolation, with computational-error tradeoff treated separately | The maximum tolerable heralded-loss boundary of that model, not an unheralded leakage rate. Origin: `stace2009loss`. |
| `0.133%` | Two-dimensional Toric code; equal independent data and syndrome error probabilities; Harrington cellular automaton with finite communication speed | A local-decoder benchmark under a restrictive symmetric phenomenological model, not the capability of global matching. Origin: `breuckmann2017local`. |

These rows are deliberately heterogeneous. Their purpose is to prevent a
reader from ranking decoders or hardware using incomparable scalars.

heading_path: Which threshold does a Toric number refer to?
Other transitions that are not decoder thresholds
chunks.markdown:
## Other transitions that are not decoder thresholds

Coherent information can exhibit an information-theoretic transition without
choosing a decoder. `lee2025coherent` derives an exact Toric coherent-information
expression and links it to random-bond Ising criticality. That result addresses
recoverable information, not the runtime or decision rule of MWPM, tensor
contraction, or BP-OSD.

Coherent rotations also carry phase information absent from a stochastic
Pauli channel. `bravyi2018coherent` gives an efficient Majorana simulation for
declared coherent-error models; `iverson2020coherence` proves a conditional
logical-incoherence trend and explicitly does not extend it to fixed physical
noise strength as `L` grows. Neither result licenses replacing coherent noise
by a universal Pauli rate.

heading_path: Which threshold does a Toric number refer to?
chunks.markdown:
## Hardware is another ledger

A finite logical error per round, a two-distance comparison, a prepared-code
state fidelity, and an asymptotic decoder threshold answer different
questions. The 2026 neutral-atom Toric experiment reports repeated extraction
and a finite comparison; the Atlas records it under realizations and does not
insert it into the table above. See
[operations and realizations](operations-and-realizations.md).

heading_path: Which threshold does a Toric number refer to?
chunks.markdown:
## Citation corrections

- DOI `10.1103/Physics.5.50` resolves to an APS Physics Viewpoint. It is
  secondary commentary and not the primary origin of a numerical row.
- DOI `10.1103/PhysRev.88.1332` and DOI `10.1143/JPSJ.55.3305` are classical
  Ising-model sources. They are precursors to the statistical machinery, not
  direct Toric-code threshold reports.
- arXiv `1810.09621` concerns measurement-based fault tolerance beyond
  foliation; its placement near a threshold feature does not make it a Toric
  code-capacity benchmark.

Primary sources: `wang2010thresholds`, `bombin2012strong`, `stace2009loss`,
`breuckmann2017local`, `lee2025coherent`, `bravyi2018coherent`, and
`iverson2020coherence`.

card.description: The square Toric code puts one qubit on every edge of an L-by-L periodic square cellulation. Vertex X stars and face Z plaquettes detect endpoints of open error strings. Contractible closed strings are stabilizers, while the two independent primal cycles and their crossing dual cycles form two logical Pauli pairs. This entry is the static two-dimensional qubit family, not an open Surface patch, a higher-dimensional Toric code, or every model in the same topological phase.

operations.cost: one parallel physical-Pauli layer on a noncontractible length-L support, or a classical Pauli-frame update

origin.method: constructor logical-loop commutation, row-space, and symplectic-pair checks

operations.cost: one pairwise physical-CNOT layer; alignment, transport, and correlated decoding are external architecture costs
operations.gate: CNOT between corresponding logical sectors of two aligned Toric blocks

operations.cost: fold pairings, Dehn-twist deformation, and single-shot logical Pauli measurements with protocol-specific ancillas and decoding
single-shot measurement gadget plus an ancilla layout and decoder from the proposed Toric Clifford protocol

params.L: Integer linear size L >= 2 of the periodic square fundamental domain; there are L^2 vertices, L^2 faces, and 2 L^2 edge qubits.

realizations.description: The experiment prepared and characterized a finite Toric-code state on periodic geometry. This establishes state preparation, not repeated syndrome extraction, arbitrary logical-state preservation, or below-threshold scaling.
realizations.platform: reconfigurable neutral-atom array with coherent transport

realizations.description: Repeated Toric syndrome extraction, lost-qubit replacement, reservoir reloading, and decoded logical-memory data were demonstrated. The reported finite two-distance comparison remains bound to its stated round range and is not promoted as an asymptotic threshold.
realizations.platform: neutral-atom array with mid-circuit measurement and atom reloading

relations.how: HGP(C_L, C_L^T), where C_L is the square cyclic neighbor-parity map, reproduces the ordered Toric check matrices exactly. These periodic square factors are not the open rep_L factors used by the planar Surface construction recipe.

Both use the square-lattice star and plaquette bulk. Cutting the torus creates rough and smooth boundaries and changes absolute cycles into relative strings; closing those boundaries restores two periodic homology directions. Bulk equivalence is not code-space identity.

At the appropriate frames, contracting the just-measured Honeycomb matching and applying a depth-one local Clifford basis change gives Toric stabilizers on a coarser lattice. The full Honeycomb object remains a time-periodic measurement protocol with spacetime detectors and an anyon automorphism.

views.description: Expanding every vertex star and face boundary gives sparse binary X and Z matrices. Their stacked symplectic rows are the executable baseline for commutation, rank, exact small-instance distance, logical-loop, and stacked-block CNOT checks.

Qubits are the one-cells of a square cellulation of the torus. The face boundary d2 and vertex incidence d1 satisfy d1 d2=0; HX=d1 and HZ=d2^T. Cycles modulo local boundaries leave the two noncontractible homology directions and hence two logical qubits.

Let C_L be the square cyclic repetition parity map with one check per periodic neighbor pair. HGP(C_L, C_L^T) reproduces the constructor's ordered star and plaquette matrices exactly. The square cyclic factors have both kernel and transpose-kernel sectors; this is why the output has two logical sectors, unlike HGP of the open repetition factors used by the planar Surface entry.

Open primal and dual strings create endpoint excitations of the two charge types. Closed contractible strings act locally, while crossing noncontractible strings have odd symplectic intersection and therefore realize conjugate logical Paulis.

Corrections with one syndrome split into homology classes whose total likelihoods become disorder-sector partition functions. Matching keeps a light representative; maximum-likelihood decoding compares class free energies. The phase boundary depends on the noise and syndrome model.

A PEPS virtual Z2 symmetry encodes the same topological degeneracy and local indistinguishability. In decoding, tensor contractions instead sum probabilities inside logical classes; the state representation and the decoder use related mathematics but answer different questions.

Under restricted coherent-noise channels the correction calculation can be mapped to free Majorana fermions and simulated efficiently. This is a channel-specific algorithmic dictionary, not a claim that the physical qubits are tetrons or that arbitrary coherent noise becomes Pauli noise.
